title: 10 Dishes That Explain Brasília
description: A capital assembled from many migrations: candango counter food, Northeastern carne de sol, Japanese and Peruvian kitchens, Cerrado accents and dining rooms shaped by political and civic life.

cards.title: Pizza dupla — Lanchonete Dom Bosco
cards.subtitle: Two rectangular mozzarella slices folded together at the 107 Sul counter.
cards.notes: This stripped-down order—pizza doubled into a handheld sandwich—captures the quick counter meals that grew alongside the new capital. The house still centers its identity on one simple pizza rather than an expansive menu.
cards.short_summary: Brasília’s modernist scale meets its compact counter lunch: two slices, one paper plate and no ceremony.
cards.source_title: Aniversário de Brasília: 66 rolês gastronômicos para fazer na capital — Metrópoles

cards.title: Carne de sol — Xique-Xique
cards.subtitle: Carne de sol with feijão-de-corda, macaxeira, rice, paçoca and manteiga de garrafa.
cards.notes: Xique-Xique links the Asa Sul superquadras to Caicó and the wider Northeast. The complete plate makes visible the food traditions carried by migrants who built and populated Brasília.
cards.short_summary: A Northeastern migration story served complete, down to paçoca and bottled butter.
cards.source_title: Sabores do sertão: veja um roteiro para comer uma boa carne de sol — Correio Braziliense

cards.title: Quibe assado à Beirute — Bar Beirute
cards.subtitle: The 109 Sul institution’s returning house-style baked kibbeh.
cards.notes: Beirute began as an Arab restaurant and became a durable meeting place for Brasília’s mixed social and cultural circles. Its named quibe shows how immigrant cooking can become part of a young city’s own memory.
cards.short_summary: An Arab-Brazilian bar staple tied to one of the capital’s long-running communal rooms.
cards.source_title: Veja onde comer um verdadeiro banquete árabe em Brasília — Correio Braziliense

cards.title: Sukiyaki — New Koto
cards.subtitle: Beef, tofu, shiitake and vegetables with udon, served in an iron pot.
cards.notes: New Koto’s hot-pot dish points to Brasília’s unusually strong Japanese diplomatic and culinary thread: founder Ryozo Komiya previously cooked for Japan’s embassy. It is also a useful counterweight to the city’s familiar sushi shorthand.
cards.short_summary: A shared iron pot reflects the Japanese expertise embedded in the diplomatic capital.
cards.source_title: New Koto — VEJA Brasília Comer & Beber

cards.title: Ceviche Lago Sul — Taypá
cards.subtitle: Tuna, avocado, lychee, nori and cucumber in a sweet-sour truffled leche de tigre.
cards.notes: This Brasília-named ceviche keeps the Peruvian technique visible while folding in cosmopolitan ingredients. It speaks to a city where international communities are everyday neighbors rather than an occasional theme.
cards.short_summary: Peruvian form and Brasília-facing invention meet in a ceviche named for Lago Sul.

cards.title: Filé Vinho e Mel — Restaurante Universal
cards.subtitle: A long-running house classic explicitly listed by the Asa Sul restaurant.
cards.notes: Universal’s sweet-savory fillet represents the author-driven dining rooms that helped Brasília develop a restaurant identity beyond imported regional traditions. Its longevity on the house’s classics list matters more than novelty.
cards.short_summary: A named house classic from the generation that gave Brasília its own contemporary dining voice.
cards.source_title: Restaurante Universal — Cardápio e Clássicos Universal

cards.title: Tábua de picanha fatiada — Fogo de Chão Brasília
cards.subtitle: Sliced picanha presented as a sharing board on the Brasília menu.
cards.notes: The board places churrasco in Brasília’s lakefront, institutional landscape: a southern Brazilian format recast for the capital’s large-table lunches and cross-regional population.
cards.short_summary: A shareable churrasco cut shows how Brasília gathers Brazil’s regional tables into one city.
cards.source_title: Cardápio Entrada Brasília — Fogo de Chão Brasil

cards.title: Steak tartare de carne de sol — Casa Baco
cards.subtitle: Parrilla-seared carne de sol with pequi aioli, tucupi, maxixe pickle and baru.
cards.notes: The dish crosses a French preparation with sertão curing and ingredients from the Cerrado and Amazon. That deliberate mixture mirrors Brasília itself: regional traditions meet here without collapsing into a single “typical” cuisine.
cards.short_summary: Carne de sol, pequi, tucupi and baru turn a European format into a map of Brazilian migration.
cards.source_title: Sabores do sertão: veja um roteiro para comer uma boa carne de sol — Correio Braziliense

cards.title: Juazeiro — Gibão Carne de Sol
cards.subtitle: Carne de sol with rice, feijão-de-corda, cassava, paçoca, vinaigrette and bottled butter.
cards.notes: Named for a sertão city and built for sharing, Juazeiro makes Brasília’s Northeastern inheritance legible through the complete grammar of a carne-de-sol meal—not just the protein.
cards.short_summary: A communal sertão platter preserves the accompaniments that give carne de sol its cultural context.
cards.source_title: Sabores do sertão: veja um roteiro para comer uma boa carne de sol — Correio Braziliense

cards.title: Riso Maremonti — Bloco C Restaurante
cards.subtitle: Brothy rice with fresh shrimp, mascarpone and Prosciutto di Parma.
cards.notes: Created for the 2026 Boa Lembrança collection, this rice dish illustrates Brasília’s contemporary international register: Italian references and Brazilian restaurant culture meet in a city built around exchange.
cards.short_summary: A current Brasília creation translates the capital’s outward-looking character into a composed rice dish.
cards.source_title: Boa Lembrança 2026: veja a lista completa dos 98 pratos do ano — Correio Braziliense
